item.title: While Surging to Records, Stocks Experience Some ‘Wobbles’
item.description: Beneath the S&P 500’s 2 percent gain in the third quarter, the rise in oil prices and bond yields led some investors to become more cautious about the outlook for A.I. profits.

item.title: Trump Media’s Merger With Nuclear Fusion Company Moves Closer to Completion
item.description: A securities filing laid out the terms of the deal between Truth Social’s parent company and TAE Technologies, which was formally announced in December.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Goldstein
item.media:description: President Trump would own a little over 20 percent of Trump Media’s stock after the company merged with TAE Technologies, according to a regulatory filing.

item.title: Fed’s Watchdog Finds No Misconduct or Illegal Activity in Costly Renovations
item.description: A new report by the Federal Reserve’s independent inspector general concluded that a nearly $2.5 billion construction project was poorly managed but made no referrals to the U.S. attorney general.
item.dc:creator: Colby Smith
item.media:description: Renovations to the Federal Reserve became a flashpoint between President Trump and Jerome H. Powell before Mr. Powell stepped down as the central bank’s chair in May.

item.title: E.E.O.C. Sues Harvard for Data on Diversity in Hiring Practices
item.description: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission filed a lawsuit asking a judge to compel the university to provide information on hiring practices that the agency said discriminated against white men.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Davis O’Brien and Michael C. Bender
item.media:credit: Sophie Park for The New York Times
item.media:description: Harvard has been a frequent target of federal officials under the Trump administration.

item.title: Google Wants Hollywood to Stop Being So Afraid of Technology

item.title: Medical Records Firm Uses AI Tool to Expose Flaws that Threaten Patient Privacy

item.title: Condé Nast C.E.O. Leaves to Run Mattel
item.description: Roger Lynch, who has led the publisher for more than seven years, will become the chief executive of the toy company, he said Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Katie Robertson
item.media:description: Roger Lynch said in a memo to Condé Nast employees that he was stepping down as chief executive to run the toymaker Mattel.

item.title: Fed’s Preferred Inflation Gauge Points to Continued Price Pressures
item.description: The Personal Consumption Expenditures price index showed little sign of easing in August, though revised data showed inflation had been slightly cooler than previously believed.
item.dc:creator: Ben Casselman and Colby Smith
item.media:credit: Anna Rose Layden for The New York Times
item.media:description: The immediate question confronting Federal Reserve officials, led by Kevin M. Warsh, is how quickly they need to deliver additional rate increases in order to firm their grip on inflation.

item.title: Bracing for More Inflation Volatility

item.title: DeepSeek and Huawei Target a Key Source of Nvidia’s A.I. Dominance

item.title: Trump’s New Tariffs Get a Familiar Day in Court

item.media:description: Despite two years of economic shocks and uncertainty, President Trump still sees sky-high tariffs as potent economic tools for his policies.

item.title: How to Listen to Your Favorite Music, Online or Off the Grid

item.title: He Was a Tech Investor Before There Was a Silicon Valley

item.title: Troubles at Situational Awareness Point to Record Stock Market Leverage

item.media:description: Big banks lent Leopold Aschenbrenner’s firm billions to invest in the artificial intelligence boom. Then the firm had a meltdown.

item.title: A.I. Is ‘Better Informed’ Than Doctors, Kennedy Tells Industry-Backed MAHA Summit

item.title: X2, Troubled Six Flags Roller Coaster, to Close After Lawsuits
